judged_text: Anonymous users can make the forum scrape and publish arbitrary pages of the embeddable host — the embed controller enqueues retrieve_topic with a fully user-controlled embed_url before any validation, and the job only checks URI(embed_url).host == embeddable_host leaving the path unrestricted, bypassing all posting permissions/trust levels by publishing as the configured embed_by_username user; the 60s throttle is per-URL so unlimited distinct URLs also flood sidekiq and hammer the host

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows unauthenticated access to `EmbedController#best` (no auth guard) which, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with `params[:embed_url]` (user-controlled) (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only verifies `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and does not constrain path/query (lib/topic_retriever.rb), so any URL under that host can be fetched server-side via `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The import creates/updates posts as the configured `embed_by_username` user and uses `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: :raw_html` (TopicEmbed.import + Post.cook change), effectively bypassing normal posting validation gates. Throttling is keyed by full URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many distinct URLs can bypass the 60s throttle and flood Sidekiq / hammer the host (lib/topic_retriever.rb). While the controller does validate the *referer host* in `ensure_embeddable`, it does not validate that `embed_url` corresponds to the referer, so the abuse path remains.
